patch_description:
This ansatz retains the strongest lesson from the prior results—global parameter sharing and parameter-free entanglement—but replaces the Möbius ladder and trainable Ising network with a distinct interleaved hypercube construction. Three disjoint CZ matchings connect qubits according to the three bit-flip dimensions of a 3-dimensional hypercube, giving diameter-three information propagation aligned with the fixed three block repetitions.

Instead of placing all entanglers in one commuting layer, the matchings are separated by collective noncommuting RY, RZ, and RX rotations. RY and RX share one mixer parameter, while RZ uses one phase parameter, leaving only two circuit parameters and four total trainable parameters including readout calibration. This preserves parameter economy while producing richer repeated dynamics, balanced connectivity, and strong symmetry-based regularization for few-shot generalization.
